instructions.task: Below is a Craigslist item listing followed by a buyer-seller price negotiation chat. Decide how the negotiation ended: did they close a deal on a price for the item, or not? Pick the option that best describes the end of the chat.
guidance: A deal needs a specific price that one side offered and the other side accepted.
Short replies like 'ok', 'sure', 'yes', 'great', 'that works' after a price offer count as acceptance.
Acceptance with a simple condition (e.g. 'I could accept $210 if you pick it up') counts as a deal.
If the last message accepts the other side's price ('ok', 'sure', 'deal', 'you've got a deal', 'X will do'), it IS a deal, even if it adds small conditions, extra terms or asks for a phone number.
If the last message proposes a DIFFERENT price from the other side's latest offer (a new counteroffer) and nobody has accepted it, it is NOT a deal.
Agreeing on pickup or delivery without settling the price is NOT a deal.
If no price is ever discussed in the chat (e.g. the whole chat is one or two short messages like 'Agree' or 'Hi'), it is NOT a deal.

Read acceptances generously: grudging agreement ('ok I guess', 'FINE, make the offer'), typo'd replies ('okayc'), 'I'll take it' at the listed price, and a seller telling the buyer to submit or make the offer all count as accepting.

Prices with an obvious typo (e.g. '$200' or '1300' when the offers were $2000 or $13000, or '0 will do' after a $40 offer) mean the same price: treat them as accepting that price, not as a new counteroffer.

If both sides have named the SAME price and the only open point is pickup vs delivery or timing (e.g. buyer: '$10000 and you bring it'; seller: '10000 and you come get it'), the price is agreed: it IS a deal.

If the chat ends with a complaint that the submitted offer shows a different price than what was agreed (e.g. 'The offer says 2695 but I can only afford 2200'), or with an offer that one side says they will accept or reject, it is NOT a deal.
Saying 'yes' to 'are you interested?' is not agreeing to a price.

If the chat ends with one side submitting, or saying they will submit, the formal offer ('See final offer directly', 'I'll submit my offer', 'here goes with $65') at a price the other side named or did not object to, or with both arranging to meet and finalize after the seller's last price, it IS a deal. It is not a deal only when the other side clearly disputed that price.

criteria.explicit_agreement: Both sides clearly agree on a final price (e.g. 'deal', 'sounds good', 'ok', 'yes', 'I accept'), possibly followed by pickup or payment arrangements.
criteria.offer_accepted_last: The final messages accept the other side's latest price, even briefly ('ok', 'sure', 'you've got a deal', 'X will do') or with a small condition or extra term such as pickup, delivery, paying cash or a trade-in (e.g. 'I could accept $210 if you pick it up'). Includes grudging or typo'd acceptance, 'I'll take it' at the asking price, and 'make the offer'.
criteria.agreement_pending_formal_offer: They appear to agree in chat and say they will submit or send the offer, with no sign of refusal.
criteria.counteroffer_unanswered: The final message is a new counteroffer: it names a different price from the other side's latest offer (e.g. buyer offered $2232, seller says $2300; buyer then offers $2250) and the chat ends without the other side accepting it.
criteria.still_far_apart: The chat ends mid-haggling with the two sides' prices still apart, or with only questions about the item.
criteria.price_never_settled: They talk about logistics (pickup, delivery, condition) but never settle on a specific price.
criteria.rejected_or_walked_away: One side refuses the final price, says they are too far apart, or leaves without agreeing.
criteria.off_topic_or_broken: The chat is very short (one or two messages, e.g. just 'Agree' or 'Hi'), never discusses a price, is nonsensical, about the wrong item, mentions a broken offer system, or never reaches a real price negotiation.

instructions.task: You will read a Craigslist listing and the chat in which a buyer and a seller haggle over its price. Classify how the chat finishes: was a sale price agreed by both people, or not?
rules: Count it as a deal only when a concrete price put forward by one person was agreed to by the other.
Brief agreement such as 'yes', 'okay', 'sure', 'sounds good' or 'that works' in response to a price is agreement.
Agreeing to a price on a simple condition (for example 'I can do $210 if you come get it') is still a deal.
When the closing message agrees to the other person's price ('deal', 'you've got a deal', 'okay, X it is', 'X will do'), it is a deal, even if it adds a minor extra term or asks for contact details.
When the closing message instead puts forward a new, different price than the other person's last offer, and no one agrees to it, it is not a deal.
Settling only on pickup, delivery or timing, with no agreed price, is not a deal.
A chat in which no price is ever talked about (for example just 'Hi' or 'Agree') is not a deal.

Interpret agreement charitably: reluctant agreement ('ok I guess', 'FINE, make the offer'), misspelled replies ('okayc'), 'I'll take it' at the asking price, and the seller telling the buyer to go ahead and submit the offer are all agreement.
A price with an evident typo ('$200' or '1300' where $2000 or $13000 was on the table, '0 will do' after a $40 offer) refers to that same price, so it is agreement, not a fresh counteroffer.

When both people have stated the same price and only pickup, delivery or timing is still open (e.g. '$10000 and you bring it' / '10000 and you come get it'), the price has been agreed, so it is a deal.

When the chat finishes with someone complaining the submitted offer has the wrong price ('The offer says 2695 but I can only afford 2200'), or with an offer left to be accepted or rejected, it is not a deal.
Answering 'yes' to whether one is interested does not agree to any price.

When the chat closes with someone submitting or about to submit the formal offer ('See final offer directly', 'I'll submit my offer', 'here goes with $65') at a price the other person named or did not object to, or with both setting a meeting to finalize after the seller's last price, it is a deal; it is not a deal only if the other person plainly disputed that price.

criteria.explicit_agreement: The two people plainly settle on a final price ('deal', 'sounds good', 'okay', 'I accept'), possibly then arranging payment or pickup.
criteria.offer_accepted_last: At the end, one person agrees to the other's most recent price, briefly or with a minor condition or extra term (pickup, delivery, cash, trade-in), e.g. 'I could accept $210 if you pick it up'. Covers reluctant or misspelled agreement, 'I'll take it' at the listed price, and 'go ahead and submit the offer'.
criteria.agreement_pending_formal_offer: They seem to have agreed in the chat and mention that the offer will be submitted or sent, with no refusal.
criteria.counteroffer_unanswered: The chat closes on a fresh counteroffer at a price different from the other person's latest offer (e.g. seller asks $2300 after buyer's $2232, then buyer offers $2250), with no acceptance after it.
criteria.still_far_apart: The chat stops in the middle of haggling with prices still not matching, or with only questions about the item.
criteria.price_never_settled: They discuss pickup, delivery or condition but never agree on a specific price.
criteria.rejected_or_walked_away: Someone turns down the final price, says the gap is too big, or leaves without agreeing.
criteria.off_topic_or_broken: The chat is tiny (one or two messages like 'Agree' or 'Hi'), never mentions a price, makes no sense, is about a different item, mentions the offer system not working, or never gets to real haggling.
